title: The sound heard 3,000 miles away 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
Could you sleep through a sound this loud? 👇

The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa in Indonesia made the loudest sound in recorded history. It was heard about 3,000 miles away, its pressure wave circled the planet for days, and it turned sunsets red around the world.

Sources: Nautilus ("The Sound So Loud That It Circled the Earth Four Times"), Oregon State University Volcano World ("Historical Eruption Sounds"), History.com ("Krakatoa erupts")

scenes.text: A sound shattered sailors' eardrums 40 miles away.
Nearly 3,000 miles away, on Rodrigues Island, it sounded like distant guns.
It was 1883. Krakatoa, a volcano in Indonesia, had exploded, killing at least 35,000 people.
But here's the strange part. Its pressure wave circled the planet, and barometers in 50 cities tracked it for 5 days.
Ash turned skies red, and New York fire engines rushed out to fight a sunset.
